units.text: INT. RESTAURANT WALK-IN FREEZER - NIGHT
Racks of frozen fish and crates of lemons.
Breath fogs.
A single bulb swings.
VIC SALERNO, fifties, camel-hair coat, sits on an upturned crate.
DOLORES KWAN, forties, apron over a black dress, stands at the door with a revolver held loosely at her side.
You'd have done better with the knife.
units.name: VIC

units.text: The knife is for fish.
units.name: DOLORES

units.text: I taught you that.
units.name: VIC

units.text: She lowers the gun an inch.
You taught me the books too. Both sets.
units.name: DOLORES

units.text: Then you know why I came.
units.name: VIC

units.text: I know why you think you did.
units.name: DOLORES

units.text: They speak at the same moment.
It was never personal.
units.name: VIC

units.text: It was always personal.
units.name: DOLORES

units.text: A long beat.
Vic stands, slow, rubbing his hands against the cold.
Open the door, Dolores. I'm freezing.
units.name: VIC

units.text: It locks from the outside, Vic.
units.name: DOLORES

units.text: She sets the revolver on a shelf of frozen lemons, steps out, and the heavy door thuds shut behind her.
